title: Nf Opt Production Parallel
objective: Measure and production-harden the maximal-order local worker crossover without replacing a faster native global path

oracles: sequential exact local result and canonical merge plan

handoff.summary: Hardened the production post-native-fallback worker crossover so its memory gate charges both measured evaluator RSS and canonical wire/per-branch peak estimates. Added inspectable useful-job and memory evidence, a decision-only benchmark mode, actual fallback/native win and RSS summaries, exact memory-boundary assertions, randomized completion equivalence, packaged graph freshness, prompt fatal cancellation, and native-first regression coverage. Fresh vector001 measured 53.668 s sequential versus 47.630 s parallel at 602 MB versus 1.286 GB; vector002 measured 254.337 s versus 281.184 s at 623 MB versus 1.280 GB on a heavily contended host. The stored three-sample vector001 median remains the stable positive fallback evidence (55.214 s versus 36.546 s), while native won both new rows by one to two orders of magnitude and therefore remains mandatory first choice.
risks: Parallel fallback speed is sensitive to host contention; vector002 did not win in the fresh loaded-host observation, so the gate remains conservative, post-native-fallback only, and makes no universal speedup claim.
The integration lane must rerun the broad native suite; the coordinator explicitly delegated that broad validation after this lane passed focused packaged-worker, strict, and architecture checks.

Supported-platform release runs should confirm the runtime-derived memory budget on Linux arm64, macOS arm64, and native Windows x64. Missing capability continues to select the sequential exact fallback.
next_steps: Cherry-pick this checkpoint into the maximal-order integration branch and run the consolidated native suite there.
Retain the v2 decision payload in the final evidence artifact so fixed evaluator RSS and branch/payload memory remain separately auditable.
